reason: The warm surroundings provide the situation for the sweat-cooling goal.
expectation: The body will be shown responding to warmth, setting up heat loss through sweating.

effect: Warmth is sensed by the skin and hypothalamus; the next step is to trigger a cooling response.
reaction: The sensory route makes the response more understandable.
reason: Sweat glands are the most direct next component for the evaporation goal.
expectation: The warming signal will activate sweat glands and wet the skin.

alternatives.reason: Skin blood flow could also contribute to heat loss, but sweat is the immediate goal.

effect: Sweating was not available yet; the warming response first widened skin vessels to bring more blood near the surface.
reaction: The automatic vessel step clarified the required sequence.
reason: The sweat glands are still the relevant component for the cooling goal.
expectation: The glands will produce sweat on the skin, ready to evaporate.

effect: The gland now releases sweat onto the skin; evaporation is the remaining cooling step.
reaction: The distinction between producing sweat and evaporating it is clear.
reason: Air at the skin shows water molecules lifting away and directly fits the evaporation goal.
expectation: Sweat will evaporate and carry heat away from the body.

effect: Evaporation cooled the body and reduced the sweat signal; the new goal is to respond to cold.
reaction: The fading signal makes the feedback response clear.
reason: The cold evening sets up the next temperature challenge.
expectation: The body will sense the colder surroundings and begin a cold response.

effect: The body senses cold and reduces sweating; it still needs to conserve and produce heat.
reaction: The separate reduction in sweat signalling makes the transition from warmth clear.
reason: Skin vessels can change blood flow near the surface, potentially reducing heat loss in the cold.
expectation: The skin vessels will narrow, reducing blood flow near the surface and conserving heat.

alternatives.reason: Muscle activity could generate heat, but conserving heat may come first.

effect: Skin vessels narrowed, reducing heat loss without producing heat; muscle is the remaining candidate for heat production.
reaction: The distinction between conserving and making heat is useful.
reason: Skeletal muscle can produce heat through shivering.
expectation: Muscle contractions will generate heat in response to cold.

effect: Shivering completes the cold response: muscle contractions use ATP and produce heat, complementing reduced heat loss through narrowed skin vessels.
reaction: The contrast between conserving heat and making it was satisfying and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the cold response was most worthwhile: the planned comparisons distinguish reduced heat loss from heat generated by muscle contractions.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial warming-signal step was relatively predictable, though it established the sensory pathway.

surprise.text: Sweat glands could not be added immediately after warming was sensed; compatibility feedback automatically widened the skin vessels first.

arbitrary.text: The required vessel-before-sweat sequence felt somewhat prescriptive: the feedback showed what to do but did not explain why sweating had to wait.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the connected warm and cold responses make the constructions useful for tracing physiological feedback, even if some ordering feels prescribed.
